simple.meaning: גִּתִּי (Gittîy) appears 10 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with kingship. The surrounding account also brings the name into death.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Joshua, 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, beginning at Joshua 13:3. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family, family line, death, kingship, city, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גִּתִּי (H1663) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows גִּתִּי through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: גִּתִּי (Gittîy) / H1663 is tracked through Joshua 13:3, 2 Samuel 6:10, 2 Samuel 6:11, 2 Samuel 15:18. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

timeline.evidenceText: from the Shihor, which is before Egypt, even to the border of Ekron northward, which is counted as Canaanite; the five lords of the Philistines; the Gazites, and the Ashdodites, the Ashkelonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites; also the Avvim,
So David would not move Yahweh’s ark to be with him in David’s city; but David carried it aside into Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house.
Yahweh’s ark remained in Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house three months; and Yahweh blessed Obed-Edom and all his house.
All his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.
Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why do you also go with us? Return, and stay with the king; for you are a foreigner, and also an exile. Return to your own place.
David said to Ittai, “Go and pass over.” Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones who were with him.

David sent the people out, a third part under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. The king said to the people, “I will also surely go out with you myself.”
There was again war with the Philistines at Gob; and Elhanan the son of Jaare-Oregim the Bethlehemite killed Goliath the Gittite’s brother, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
So David didn’t move the ark with him into David’s city, but carried it aside into Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house.
Again there was war with the Philistines; and Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.

definitions.short: a Gittite or inhabitant of Gath
definitions.full: H1663. Gitti גִּתִּי adjective, of a people , of II. גַּת 1 ; of Obed-edom 2Sam 6:10-11 , = 1Chr 13:13 ; Ittai 2Sam 15:19 , 22 ; 18:2 ; Goliath 21:19 ; 1Chr 20:5 ; plural with article as substantive, הַגִּתִּים 1Sam 15:18 the Gittites (but read הַגִּתִּי אִתַּי We Klo Kit Bu Now Archaeology i.308n .); singular with article as proper name collective הַגִּתִּי Josh 13:3 (with men of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the Awwim).
